Guardian business live. LD datePublished Thu 15 Oct 08:48 BST (first published 06.37 BST); rolling.
Headline: 'AI share sell-off drags South Korea's stock market down to six-month low; UK growth beats forecasts in August'. By Graeme Wearden and Heather Stewart.
08.44 BST entry: Kospi CLOSED down 7.5% at lowest closing level since April (six-month low), 'after a day of wild trading that briefly caused circuit breakers to be triggered. At its worst point, the Kospi was down over 9%.' Samsung Electronics -9.5%, SK Hynix -11.1% (close).
06.37 BST entry: 'In South Korea today, the KOSPI share index has plunged by over 8%'. Nikkei 225 'down by 4.5% in late trading'.
06.59 BST, Jim Reid, strategist, Deutsche Bank: 'Markets have just had an incredibly tumultuous 24 hours, as a strong US CPI print was then followed up with mounting fears around the AI trade.' Reid: 'Moreover, there's been a huge selloff in Asia overnight, with the KOSPI (-7.04%) and the Nikkei (-5.08%) both slumping, and the KOSPI even saw a circuit breaker triggered earlier given the scale of the declines.' Reid notes cost of insuring debt of AI firms such as CoreWeave rising.
Wall St Wed: S&P 500 -1.1% to 7,718.94; Nasdaq Composite -1.9% to 26,692.87. Dell -11%.
Guardian: 'The news yesterday that US inflation has jumped to 3.7% has alarmed traders, as it makes it more likely that the US Federal Reserve will raise interest rates soon - possibly even at the end of this month.'
Chris Weston, analyst, Pepperstone: 'Further evidence of right-tail inflation risk in the US has reinforced the higher-for-longer rates narrative, with sellers emerging across risk assets and interest rate-sensitive equities coming under renewed pressure.' / 'The breadth of price pressures across the CPI basket has been particularly concerning, challenging a market desperately in need of evidence of disinflation.'
BRITISH RELEVANCE: FTSE 100 down only 0.1%, 'insulated from the rout in chip stocks' as it lacks tech. Miners slide: Antofagasta -6.5%, Rio Tinto -4.2%, Anglo American -4%. Defensives bid: Haleon +2.6%, Whitbread +2.4%. Europe: DAX -0.5%, CAC -0.2%, IBEX -0.17%.
CoreWeave shares fell as much as 17% Wed; 2032 debt traded below 78 cents on the dollar; CDS pricing >50% chance of default within 5 years - ATTRIBUTED BY GUARDIAN TO BLOOMBERG (not an approved source; label as such or drop).
Kospi context: roughly doubled in H1 2026; now 'only' up 30% for 2026. Retail investors bought on margin.
Venue: IMF/World Bank Annual Meetings, Queen Sirikit National Convention Center, Bangkok. UK chancellor John Healey attending; 'pledges to stay the path'. Healey due to meet G20 central bankers and finance ministers and hold talks with Georgieva.
